findings.description: The reports_archive bucket has no server_side_encryption_configuration block, so objects (including the seeded vendor roster) are stored with SSE-S3 defaults at best, not customer-controlled KMS encryption required for a sensitive reporting archive.

No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block or explicit acl is defined for reports_archive, leaving the bucket's access posture to account defaults; without the public access block, accidental public exposure of report data cannot be prevented by configuration.

reports_archive has no logging block, so access to report data is not recorded; the audit_trail bucket exists in this file and is used as a log target elsewhere, making its omission here a gap in the audit trail.
The ledger_exports bucket contains financial ledger data but defines no server_side_encryption_configuration, so objects are not encrypted with a customer-managed KMS key.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block is defined for ledger_exports; the private ACL alone does not block future bucket policies or ACL changes from granting public access to ledger data.
ledger_exports has no logging block, so access to financial ledger exports is not captured in the audit trail.
model_artifacts stores machine-learning model artifacts with no server_side_encryption_configuration block, leaving potentially sensitive training artifacts unencrypted under a customer key.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block is defined for model_artifacts, so public exposure of model artifacts is not prevented by configuration.
ops_runbooks holds operational runbooks that frequently embed credentials and recovery procedures, yet has no server_side_encryption_configuration block.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block is defined for ops_runbooks, leaving sensitive operational documentation exposed to misconfiguration-driven public access.
ops_runbooks has no logging block, so reads of sensitive runbook content are not recorded for audit.

The audit bucket uses the log-delivery-write canned ACL, which grants write access to the S3 log delivery group; on the bucket that holds the audit trail itself this permits log data to be written or tampered with by any principal in that group, weakening integrity of security logs.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block is defined for the audit_trail bucket, so the most sensitive bucket in the file has no explicit guard against public exposure.
audit_trail has versioning and KMS encryption but no logging block of its own, so access to the audit records themselves is not logged.
